SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.35
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by an intense Raman band at 1003 cm⁻¹, the characteristic “ring-breathing” ν1(A1g) mode of a monosubstituted benzene ring. A second strong band at 708 cm⁻¹ matches the γ(C–H) out-of-plane bend that is likewise diagnostic for monosubstituted benzenes. The 1032 cm⁻¹ band is the typical in-plane C–H bending/ ring-stretching partner that accompanies the 1000 cm⁻¹ breathing mode. The medium 1604 cm⁻¹ line is the usual aromatic C=C stretch, and the 3065 cm⁻¹ band is the aromatic C–H stretch (rule GFQ-003). Strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2967, 2905 and 2871 cm⁻¹ and CH₃ deformations at 1446/1468 cm⁻¹ indicate several methyl groups attached to a sp³ carbon. Among the candidates, only tert-butylbenzene (1) possesses a monosubstituted benzene ring with three methyl groups on a tert-butyl substituent, fully accounting for the set of aromatic and intense CH₃ vibrations observed. Candidates containing sulfone, methoxy, hydroxyl or chlorine groups (4, 6, 8, 9, 10) should display additional strong S=O, C–O or C–Cl Raman bands (≈1140–1320 cm⁻¹ or ≈650 cm⁻¹) that are not convincingly present, while non-aromatic bicyclic candidates (2, 3, 5, 7) lack the diagnostic 1003/708 cm⁻¹ benzene features. Therefore candidate 1 best matches the experimental Raman spectrum.
